messages:
rahul: quick heads-up — after the kernel-affinity tweak on canary i bumped into a host-side regression: ingress p99 up from ~39ms to ~88ms, sys CPU up ~20%. Noticed during a short-req microburst.
zoe: thanks for flagging. can you dump a flame and socket stats? my hunch is more writev syscalls.
ben: pulled a trace: lots of small http2 DATA frames emitted by tokenizer, then multiple writev syscalls per request. stack: tokenize -> proxy-> writev -> epoll -> retry.
elaine: kvcache telemetry: async-write queue depth spikes and hot-shard evictions concurrently. tiny fragments seem to magnify index churn.
rahul: snippet from ferry logs (sanitized):
```
[ingress] accept stream #42
tokenizer: append 64B chunk
proxy: writev([hdr,64,ctl]) -> flush
kernel: sys_writev -> returns 3 syscalls
```
rahul: previously the proxy coalesced by stream-id within a 5ms window into a single 1kb write; kernel-affinity change tightened batching and we now see scatter.
zoe: ci-bot posted nightly perf diff: https://ci.redwood/pipelines/9456/diff/3164207890 (regression flagged).
ben: local microbench confirms: enabling proxy.buffer_by_stream_ms=8 reduces writev count -70% and brings p99 back near baseline.
elaine: mitigation options:
- short-term: enable proxy.buffer_by_stream_ms=8 (runtime flag) on canary.
- medium: make tokenizer emit 256B slices by default for small requests to reduce syscall count.
- long-term: add "write_density" heuristic to kernel-selector so it prefers kernels that tolerate more batching when socket write-rate per-host > threshold.
zoe: prefer short-term flag flip first. i'll own the roll. plan: flip on 10% canary at 3164207920, watch ingress_p99, sys_cpu, kvcache_hot_evicts for 20m. rollback if p99 > 80ms or error% > 0.5%.
rahul: experimental config change we tried locally:
```
proxy.buffer_by_stream_ms = 8
tokenizer.min_emit_size = 256
kernel_selector.hint = "balanced"
```
ben: bench numbers: buffer_by_stream_ms=8 -> p99 42ms (was 88ms), sys CPU -13%, kvcache-hot-evict -45%. tokenizer.min_emit_size=256 alone helps a bit but increases tail CPU in the tokenizer; combined is best.
elaine: adding a temp alert: kvcache.hot_evictions > 5/s during canary window.
zoe: rolling now. will post the incident summary and rollback steps to #incidents if anything spikes. tagging @ben for post-roll analysis on kernel-selector behavior.
ci-bot: perf snapshot uploaded: https://ci.redwood/snapshots/3164207890/summary (compare baseline 3164201000).
rahul: thanks team. i'll open a follow-up RFC for write_density hinting in kernel-selector + tokenizer emit-sizing tradeoffs.
